events.title: Indonesia Stock Market May Find Renewed Support On Friday
events.description: The Indonesia stock market turned lower again on Thursday, one day after snapping the two-day slide in which it had dropped almost 170 points or 2.9 percent. The Jakarta Composite Index now sits just above the 5,860-point plateau although it's likely to bounce higher again on Friday.

events.title: Japanese Market Sharply Higher
events.description: The Japanese market is trading sharply higher on Friday, snapping a six session losing streak, following the broadly positive cues from Wall Street overnight. The Nikkei 225 is moving well above the 65,500 level, with gains across most sectors led by technology and financial stocks.

events.title: Higher Open Called For Hong Kong Stock Market
events.description: The Hong Kong stock market has finished lower in back-to-back sessions, dropping more than 280 points or 1.2 percent along the way. The Hang Seng now sits just above the 24,060-point plateau although it's expected to open to the upside on Friday.

events.title: China Bourse Tipped To Open In The Green
events.description: The China stock market has moved lower in consecutive trading days, stumbling almost 100 points or 3.2 percent along the way. The Shanghai Composite Index now sits just above the 3,700-point plateau although it may find traction on Friday.

events.title: Australian Market Significantly Higher
events.description: The Australian stock market is trading significantly higher on Friday, reversing the losses in the previous two sessions, following the broadly positive cues from Wall Street overnight. The benchmark S&P/ASX 200 is moving a tad above 8,800 level, with gains across most sectors led by mining a technology stocks.

events.title: Rebound Anticipated For Taiwan Stock Market
events.description: The Taiwan stock market headed south again on Thursday, one day after ending the four-day losing streak in which it had dropped almost 1,500 points or 3.1 percent. The Taiwan Stock Exchange now sits just beneath the 47,000-point plateau although it may bounce higher again on Friday.

events.title: Singapore Stock Market Poised To Open In The Green
events.description: The Singapore stock market has finished lower in back-to-back sessions, slumping almost 30 points or 0.6 percent in that span. The STI now sits just above the 5,400-point plateau although it may halt its slide on Friday.

events.title: Malaysia Stock Market May Reverse Thursday's Losses
events.description: The Malaysia stock market on Thursday snapped the four-day winning streak in which it had collected almost 30 points or 1.8 percent. The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index now sits just shy of the 1,625-point plateau although it may bounce higher again on Friday.

events.title: Japan Stock Market May Halt Losing Streak
events.description: The Japan stock market has tracked lower in six straight sessions, slumping more than 6,240 points or 9.1 percent in that span. The Nikkei now sits just above the 64,425-point plateau although it may find traction on Friday.

events.title: South Korea Shares Overdue For Support On Friday
events.description: The South Korea stock market has finished lower in seven straight sessions, cratering more than 1,450 points or 22.5 percent along the way. The KOSPI now sits just above the 5,550-point plateau although it may stop the bleeding on Friday.

events.title: Singapore Export Data Due On Friday
events.description: Singapore will on Friday release September figures for non-oil domestic exports, highlighting a modest day for Asia-Pacific economic activity. In August, NODX rose 10.9 percent on month and 46.2 percent on year, for a trade surplus of SGD13.780 billion.

events.title: South Korea Export Prices Surge 40.9% On Year In September
events.description: Export prices in South Korea spiked 40.9 percent on year in September, the Bank of Korea said on Friday - easing from 42.7 percent in August.

events.title: New Zealand Manufacturing Sector Accelerates In September - BusinessNZ
events.description: The manufacturing sector in New Zealand continued to expand in September, and at a faster pace, the latest survey from BusinessNZ revealed on Friday with a manufacturing PMI score of 56.5.
